sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
நேசம் நிறை நேரிழையாள் மின்னிடையாள்
பாசமாய் ஓர்சொல் பகர்வேன் என்பாள்
sections.translit:
nEsam niRai nErizhaiyAL minnidaiyAL
pAsamAy Orsol pagarvEn enbAL
sections.en: My darling, with a waist as thin as a lightning bolt, would state lovingly that she has just one statement to make.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
காசிக்குப் போகாதீர் என்னுயிரே காரணம் கூறிடுவேன்
விசாலி என உயிர் விடுப்பார் என்றுரைக்கும் விஸ்வநாதரும்
ஆசை விடுத்துப் பால் நீறணிந்து புன்னை மரத்தருகே
ஓசை விடுத்து ஒரு பில்வத்துள் ஒருங்கிணைந்தார் (என்பர்)
sections.translit:
kAsikkup pOgAdhIr ennuyirE kAraNam kURiduvEn
visAli ena uyir viduppAr endRuraikkum viswanAdharum
Asai vidutthup pAl nIRaNindhu punnai marattharugE
Osai vidutthu oru bilvatthuL orungiNaindhAr (enbar)
sections.en: I will tell you the reasons but do not head to the sacred city of Kasi. Even Lord Viswanatha, whom the world says dotes on his consort Goddess Visalakshi and is willing to trade his life for her love, has given everything up. Perhaps this has something to do with the milieu in Kasi. He appears now with the spread of milky white ash on his forehead, sits under a tamanu tree (known as Alexandria larel or Calophyllum inophyllum), in a serene surrounding without any noise. People are of the opinion that He has become one with the sacred bilva leaf which he loves so much.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
மனித்த பிறவிப்பயன் பெறவே புனித காசி சென்றோரும்
கனி விடுப்பார் காய் விடுப்பார் விழைந்ததை விடுப்பார்
நெஞ்சினில் என் நினைவாய் உறைந்திடும் நீயும்
அஞ்சுகிறேன் மறந்தென்னை விடுப்பாயோ யானறியேன்
பாணிக்கிரஹணம் புரிவீர் காசியாத்திரை போவதுபோல் பாசாங்கும் செய்வீர்
காலணி வாங்கச் சொல்வேன் என் பிதாவிடம் இப்போதே
sections.translit:
manittha piRavippayan peRavE punidha kAsi sendRorum
kani viduppAr kAy viduppAr vizhaindhadhai viduppAr
nenjinil en ninaivAy uRaindhidum nIyum
anjugiREn maRandhennai viduppAyO yAnaRiyEn
pANigrahaNam purivIr kAsiyAtthirai pOvadhupOl pAsAngum seyvIr
kAlaNi vAngach cholvEn en pithAvidam ippOdhE
sections.en: People who are very religious take a pilgrimage to the sacred city of Kasi to achieve spiritual benefits. They take a dip in the Ganges river and catch a glimpse of Lord Viswanatha. They vow to give something up that they loved until now, such as a vegetable or fruit, to demonstrate their renunciation. You are constantly thinking about me. I am very scared whether you will abandon me if you go on this trip to Kasi. Marry me. Pretend as though you are really into visiting the sacred Kshetram of Kasi. As part of this religious textual event, I will ask my father to buy you the right kind of shoes that you will need to go on this trip. Remember again that this is solely a wedding ritual and learn to act the part.

notes: This song is based on the restlessness and fear of a new bride around what her husband-to-be will do during the Hindu pre-wedding ritual of Kasi Yathra, or pilgrimage. This poem subtly mocks this ritual. The prospective bride advises her fiancé to simply follow the wedding tradition. She urges him to put on a show of heading to Kasi but instead to take a short ride around the wedding venue. As part of the ritual, the bridegroom will be provided with some sacred books. She advises him not to immerse in these religious texts and renounce her in this pretend quest. She points to the historical precedent of the deity in Kasi, Sri Viswanatha, going into meditation and leaving behind his consort Visalakshi.
